collection: NCEE original vocational decision and record-reading practice
note: 24 original MCQs using historical Primary 6 references, including two new provisional sewing/construction mappings. Written choices do not assess practical performance. Four options and one mark are author practice choices, not an official NCEE task-family or marking claim. All questions remain academic-review pending.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish temporary, permanent and decorative stitches and choose a stitch purpose for a stated task.
questions.prompt: A pupil wants to hold two pieces of fabric together for a fitting, then remove those stitches after checking the position. Which class of stitch suits that purpose?
options: Temporary
Permanent
Decorative only
A painted line
questions.answer: Temporary
questions.explanation: Temporary stitching holds pieces for an intermediate step and is intended to be removed.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one practice mark are author choices. Historical Primary 6 reference alignment is provisional; official NCEE task families and full blueprint remain unverified. Written reasoning does not demonstrate practical sewing, cleaning or food preparation.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish temporary, permanent and decorative stitches and choose a stitch purpose for a stated task.
questions.prompt: A cloth bag needs stitching that will remain in place while the bag is used. Which property matters most for that stitching?

It is visible only in a photograph.
It changes colour whenever the bag moves.
It secures the fabric pieces for continued use.
questions.answer: It secures the fabric pieces for continued use.
questions.explanation: Permanent stitching is intended to remain and hold the material together.

questions.learningObjective: Explain the purpose of a seam and reason about a simple construction sequence.
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a seam in a cloth shopping bag?
options: To join pieces of fabric.
To measure the length of the handles.
To store unused thread.
To choose the colour of the bag.
questions.answer: To join pieces of fabric.
questions.explanation: A seam is a join between fabric pieces, usually secured by stitching.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Explain the purpose of a seam and reason about a simple construction sequence.
questions.prompt: A pupil is joining two marked fabric edges in a supervised lesson. Which sequence is most reasonable?
options: Stitch at random, then look for the edges.
Cut away every marking before checking the position.
Pull the pieces apart before securing any part.
Align the edges, hold them in position, then stitch along the marked line.
questions.answer: Align the edges, hold them in position, then stitch along the marked line.
questions.explanation: Alignment and temporary holding help keep the join in the intended position.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select packaging for a purpose and interpret simple farm records.
questions.prompt: A school garden sends soft ripe tomatoes in a sack with heavy pumpkins placed above them. Which change best addresses the packaging problem?
options: Pack the tomatoes separately in a container that prevents the heavy produce from crushing them.
Put more pumpkins on top to keep the sack still.
Remove the tomatoes’ labels but keep the same arrangement.
Tie the sack tighter around all the produce.
questions.answer: Pack the tomatoes separately in a container that prevents the heavy produce from crushing them.
questions.explanation: Packaging must protect the produce during transport; separating a fragile item from heavy loads addresses the stated risk.

questions.learningObjective: Select packaging for a purpose and interpret simple farm records.
questions.prompt: A package is labelled “large basket” although it contains only a small bundle hidden by an oversized cover. What is the best improvement?
options: Hide the quantity label on the bottom.
Call every bundle a large basket regardless of its contents.
Use packaging and a description that show the actual quantity honestly.
Add a brighter cover while keeping the misleading description.
questions.answer: Use packaging and a description that show the actual quantity honestly.
questions.explanation: Packaging should identify and present the goods without misleading the buyer.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select packaging for a purpose and interpret simple farm records.
questions.prompt: A club is choosing between an attractive weak carton and a plain strong carton for moving produce. The weak carton tears under the load. Which decision best fits the transport purpose?
options: Remove part of the strong carton’s base to make it look lighter.
Use the sound carton that supports the load, adding clear identification if needed.
Use the torn carton because appearance is the only purpose of packaging.
Leave both cartons outdoors until their labels fade.
questions.answer: Use the sound carton that supports the load, adding clear identification if needed.
questions.explanation: Transport suitability and identification matter; appearance cannot compensate for failure to hold the produce.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select packaging for a purpose and interpret simple farm records.
questions.prompt: The garden diary records that a storm damaged a fence. The cash record has no entry for a repair. Which conclusion is justified?
options: The absence of a payment proves no damage happened.
The fence must have repaired itself.
The club certainly paid a particular amount in cash.
The diary records damage, but a repair payment cannot be established from these records.
questions.answer: The diary records damage, but a repair payment cannot be established from these records.
questions.explanation: Different records supply different evidence; missing payment evidence does not prove the physical event did not occur.

questions.prompt: Two teams must clean the same room, but neither knows which tables have already been wiped. Which plan best avoids repeated work and missed tables?

Wipe only whichever table is nearest the door.
Agree areas for each team and mark tasks complete after checking them.
Let both teams start anywhere without speaking.

questions.learningObjective: Choose tools and an order of work suited to a cleaning job.
questions.prompt: A pupil wants to wipe a wooden shelf but is unsure whether the provided cleaning agent is suitable for its finish. What is the best next step?
options: Pour the agent over the books first.
Ask the supervising adult to check suitability before applying it.
Use the strongest agent available without checking.
Mix all the agents together to make one cleaner.
questions.answer: Ask the supervising adult to check suitability before applying it.
questions.explanation: Matching the cleaning agent to the material avoids inappropriate treatment; uncertainty should be resolved before use.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select meals or menu descriptions that meet stated needs and constraints.
questions.prompt: A fictional meal-planning exercise gives these lunch costs: rice and beans ₦700; yam and vegetables ₦850; noodles and egg ₦950; plantain and beans ₦800. The budget is ₦900 and the chosen meal must include yam. Which choice meets both stated conditions?
options: Yam and vegetables
Rice and beans
Noodles and egg
Plantain and beans
questions.answer: Yam and vegetables
questions.explanation: Yam and vegetables includes the required yam and costs less than ₦900. The other meals either lack yam or exceed the limit.

Remove the evening line so the missing plan is hidden.

questions.explanation: A specific meal entry communicates what is planned; vague wording does not.

questions.prompt: A household has ingredients for bean porridge, but the planned menu requires an ingredient that cannot be obtained today. Which response shows practical meal planning?
options: Stop checking ingredients for future meals.
Revise the menu using available ingredients while considering the household’s needs.
Keep the menu unchanged and pretend the missing ingredient is available.
Spend the whole budget on printing a new menu cover.

questions.explanation: Meal planning considers resources and availability as well as the written menu.
